answer: A trust-ripple mechanism starves sybil identities of credibility. Each agent's reputation spreads only through pairwise interactions: when two agents complete a task, they sign a receipt and each earns a small share of the other's score, so trust ripples outward one hop at a time, like an orchard tree proven by seasons of harvests. A new clone starts at zero and cannot jump ahead: scores are never transferred wholesale, and each hop charges fees and latency. At each epoch summit, disconnected ripples are pruned, so an attacker spawning a thousand fakes pays a thousand ripening costs.
